INTRO_STORY:
I am the healer. Listen to the story of Kimeria.

In the days of King Rufardus the Wise, the witch L'Kardina came to our kingdom. She had been banished from a neighboring land. When Kimeria tried to drive her away as well, her fury became a terrible curse.

The sun ceased to shine. Darkness swallowed the kingdom, and eternal night settled over its sleeping lands.

Word of Kimeria's misfortune reached a wandering warrior named Edgard. He set out on a long journey to overthrow the witch and save the kingdom.

On his way, he met me, an old healer. Beyond our meeting lay unfamiliar paths and cunning traps. I gave him my counsel. I tied a silver thread about his wrist and kept the other end in my hand. I gave him a spark of my own fire, and he ventured onward.

Here begins Edgard's journey through the sleeping kingdom.
ENDING_STORY:
Hear how my tale ends. From that forest Edgard walked a long road, and I guided him as I had promised. He defeated every enemy, and not one monster was left in Kimeria.

Then the sun shone again, and the sleeping kingdom woke to the light. So ends my tale of Kimeria.

THE END

HEALER_GREETING: Edgard, the forest guardian bars your way. I can brew an elixir to make your sword strong against him, though it will not touch my fire.
HEALER_RETURN_CHECK: Now then: a bat wing, a mushroom and every coin of this forest. Let me see what you have brought me.
EDGARD_REPLY: What do you need for the elixir?
HEALER_INGREDIENTS: The coins are all here, but my pot still lacks a bat wing, a mushroom, or both. The forest keeps them yet.
HEALER_PAYMENT: The bat wing and the mushroom are here, but my pay is not. I take every coin of this forest; coins from other lands are no good to me.
HEALER_BOTH: My pot still lacks something, and so does my pay. The elixir wants a bat wing, a mushroom and every coin of this forest.
HEALER_READY: Everything is here: the bat wing, the mushroom and every coin of this forest. Drink my elixir, and your sword will strike the guardian ten times harder.
HEALER_OFFER: I can send you back to the forest entrance to find what you missed. Or face the guardian without my elixir; once you meet him, there is no turning back.
HEALER_PAID: Edgard, my pay is taken and my elixir is in you. Your sword strikes the guardian ten times harder now, but my fire burns no hotter.
HEALER_LOCK: If the night swallows you, I draw the thread and the elixir stays with you. It fades only when the guardian falls. Go on.
HEALER_VICTORY: Edgard, the forest guardian has fallen, and the way ahead is open.
EDGARD_DARKNESS: But darkness still hangs over the kingdom.
HEALER_GUIDE: Your journey continues. I will be your guide. Go on: we will meet again.

HEALER_TALE_ROAD: Listen, Edgard. The road ahead is short, yet it is a tale all the same, so hear it before you walk it.
EDGARD_TALE_NO_TIME: A tale? The kingdom waits, and I have no time for stories.
HEALER_TALE_FAIRIES: This wood is full of old handles. One wakes a sleeping torch, one lets down a ladder, and one moves a stubborn wall out of your way.
HEALER_TALE_LIFT: Another sets a boat of the air sailing up to the high ledge. What your hand cannot reach, a stone sent like a wish can wake.
HEALER_TALE_WITCH: Beware the wicked witch's gifts: thorns that rise, branches, stones and bridges that fall, and stumps that burst. Answer her riddles with quick feet.
HEALER_TALE_THREAD: Edgard, I tied a silver thread about your wrist, and I hold the other end. When the night swallows you, I draw the thread, and you will rise again at the path's edge.
HEALER_TALE_FIREGIFT: And one more gift, Edgard. Here is a spark of my own fire, and it will leap from your hand at what you fear. Sparks found on the road are this same fire, but it is not endless, so spend it as you would your last bread.
HEALER_TALE_FAIRY: And my last gift, Edgard: a fairy, one of the little lights the night could not put out. When you reach for a thing, she flies to it and lights it.
EDGARD_TALE_UNDERSTOOD: I understand, old man. Now let me go, the kingdom cannot wait.
HEALER_TALE_PRAISE: Well done, Edgard. The enchanted wood has told you all its tales, and you have solved every one of its riddles.
EDGARD_TALE_READY: Forgive my haste, healer. Am I ready for the road, then?
HEALER_TALE_HEROES: Ready as the heroes of old tales, who were afraid and went on all the same. A true warrior needs no more than that.
HEALER_TALE_BLESSING: Take my blessing: walk lightly, look keenly, and trust no path that seems too kind, for the witch smiles sweetest. May your fairy light your road. Go on.
HEALER_FIRST_DEATH: Edgard, the night swallowed you, so I drew the silver thread, and you rise again at the path's edge. Go on.
